title: NRI Tax Residency in India: Understanding the 182-Day Rule, ₹15 Lakh Threshold
description: Indian tax residency for individuals is primarily determined by physical stay in India during a financial year. The standard Non-Resident Indian (NRI) status .

faq.q: What is the 182-day rule for NRI tax residency?
faq.a: The 182-day rule is the primary test. An individual is considered a tax resident in India if they stay in India for 182 days or more during a financial year (April 1 to March 31). If they stay for less than 182 days, they are generally classified as a Non-Resident Indian (NRI).

faq.q: How does the ₹15 lakh income threshold affect NRI residency?
faq.a: For Indian citizens or Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) visiting India, if their Indian-sourced income (excluding foreign income) exceeds ₹15 lakh in a financial year, the standard 182-day rule can be replaced by a 120-day rule. They become resident if they stay 120 days or more in the current year AND 365 days or more in the preceding four years.

Deemed residency applies to an Indian citizen whose Indian-sourced income (excluding foreign income) exceeds ₹15 lakh and who is not liable to tax in any other country due to domicile, residence, or similar criteria. Such an individual is deemed a resident of India, regardless of their physical stay.

faq.q: Is foreign income taxable for a "deemed resident"?
faq.a: No. An individual who is a "deemed resident" is automatically classified as a Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR). As an RNOR, only their Indian-sourced income and income from a business controlled in or profession set up in India are taxable in India; their other foreign income is exempt.

faq.q: Are NRIs exempt from filing Income Tax Returns (ITR) in India?
faq.a: An NRI may be exempt from filing an ITR if their total income in India consists only of investment income or long-term capital gains, or both, and the tax due on such income has been fully deducted at source (TDS).

faq.q: Is interest from NRE/FCNR accounts taxable in India for NRIs?
faq.a: No, interest earned on Non-Resident External (NRE) accounts and Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) accounts is fully exempt from income tax for NRIs.
